118350.name: Chabad House in Miami Beach and Chabad House on Wheels
118350.note: Miami Herald (COLlive, 24 July 2011): 'Katz's RV ministry, Chabad on Wheels, started 12 years ago, when he was completing rabbinical school in New York' (count back: 1999); 'Katz has opened a bricks-and-mortar synagogue on Lincoln Lane'. IRS: 'Chabad House On Wheels', Rabbi Zev Katz, ruling June 2002.

290969.name: Chabad of N.E. Hollywood & Dania
290969.note: IRS (ProPublica): 'Chabad Of North East Hollywood-Dania Inc', care of Menachem M Tennenhaus, exempt from May 2005, so it existed by then. Miami Herald (CrownHeights.info, 27 May 2007): its first Torah; 'the Hollywood Women's Club at 501 N. 14th Ave., where the synagogue conducts its services' (also called the Shul of the Lakes). Start year not found yet; lead: therebbesimpact.com 2004.

1335573.name: Chabad of Clay County
1335573.note: First Coast Chabad blog (8 March 2011) announced the new Clay County center, the first Jewish institution of any kind in the county, with Rabbi Shmuly and Shaina Feldman. Clay Today (CrownHeights.info, 22 June 2011): 'Since the Feldmans moved to Fleming Island in April they have hosted several events'.

1241523.name: Chabad of Clearwater
1241523.note: TampaBay.com (CrownHeights.info, 30 Oct 2011): 'A 600-square-foot space nestled in a cluster of offices off Gulf-to-Bay Boulevard is slowly materializing into ... a new Chabad center, the third in Pinellas County'; 'The Clearwater center will celebrate its grand opening at 1 p.m. Sunday.' Rabbi Levi and Miriam Hodakov had been program directors at Chabad of Pinellas (Palm Harbor) since 2006. Then the Tabacinic Chabad Center (2014) and the former Bank of America on Belleair Road (2023).

earlier.where: a 600-square-foot office space off Gulf-to-Bay Boulevard

1274159.name: Chabad Jewish Center of West Boynton and West Lake Worth
1274159.note: IRS (ProPublica): 'Chabad Lubavitch Of West Boynton Beach Inc', care of Yosef Raichik, exempt from Sept 2011, so it existed by then. Chabad of Greater Boynton's history: the Raichiks were hired as adult education and youth directors and 'charged with opening the satellite Chabad center in West Boynton'. Start year not found yet; lead: the chabad.org listing is from about 2010.

1269573.name: Las Olas Chabad Jewish Center
1269573.note: Chabad.org (22 Nov 2011): 'Last December, Rabbi Chaim and Chaya Mushka Slavaticki moved to Fort Lauderdale, Fla., to open a new Chabad-Lubavitch center'; they were 'getting ready to open the doors to a rented storefront they're calling the Chabad Jewish Center of Fort Lauderdale Beach'. Now at 1302 East Las Olas Blvd. (a new building proposed at 1404 E Las Olas, Nov 2025).

earlier.where: a rented storefront, the 'Chabad Jewish Center of Fort Lauderdale Beach'

2480687.name: Chabad of the Emerald Coast
2480687.note: Destin Log (CrownHeights.info, 13 Oct 2013): 'Chabad-Lubavitch recently opened a new branch on Florida's Emerald Coast. Rabbi Shaya Tenenboim, 31, who arrived from south Florida with his family just before the High Holidays' (Rosh Hashanah 5774: 5 Sept 2013); 'At this point I'm a rabbi in the local synagogue, Beth Israel of Destin'.

earlier.where: Beth Israel of Destin (as its rabbi)

427844.name: Chabad of Lake Worth
427844.note: Shmais.com (CrownHeights.info, 5 July 2006): 'Rabbi and Mrs. Mendy and Leah Rosenfeld of New Haven CT will IYH be moving on Shlichus to East Lake Worth, Florida where they will establish Chabad of Green Acres and Atlantis.' IRS: 'Chabad Of East Lake Worth Greenacres And Atlantis Inc' (care of Menachem M Rosenfeld), exempt from Feb 2008.

300767.name: Chabad of NW Coral Springs (the Chai Center)
300767.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 1 Sept 2015), on the Chai Center/Chabad of Coral Springs: Rabbi Hershy and Chanie Bronstein 'have led this Chabad center in the city for the past decade, starting with small prayer gatherings in their apartment. Then they moved into a 1,300-square-foot storefront property'; the 9,500-square-foot building (5761 Coral Ridge Drive) opened 13 Aug 2015. Count back: about 2005.

earlier.where: a 1,300-square-foot storefront near the present building

2706607.name: Chabad at Monterra
2706607.note: COLlive (its first Torah): 'Established in 2013, Chabad at Monterra has been servicing the needs of the fast-growing Jewish community'; Rabbi Adi and Malky Goodman. COLlive (16 March 2024): it 'celebrated its 10th anniversary'. IRS: 'Chabod At Monterra Inc', exempt from Aug 2014.

118534.name: Chabad @ University of Miami
118534.note: Chabad.org (23 Feb 2015): 'Rabbi Mendy Fellig opened the Chabad House at the University of Miami in Coral Gables, Fla., with his wife, Henchi, in 2001'; at 1251 Hardee Rd. by 2011. An earlier Chabad House at UM: Wikipedia, 'In 1973, Eliezrie established the Chabad House at the University of Miami' (Rabbi David Eliezrie, later of Orange County); a Miami Herald report of 14 June 1974 announced its 'rap center'. Nothing found shows it ran without a break until 2001, so the year is the Felligs' opening and 1973 is kept under 'earlier'. (Was 1973, medium, before Nov 6.)

earlier.where: an earlier Chabad House at the University of Miami (Rabbi David Eliezrie)

2739542.name: Congregation Judea Chabad
2739542.note: Lubavitch.com (11 Sept 2019), Rabbi Joseph Bronstein: 'On April 29, 2009, I became the rabbi of the newly called Congregation Judea in Hollywood, FL'; 'This is the Temple Judea that later became Congregation Judea Chabad'; 'Chabad' was added to the name four or five years after the shul became Orthodox. The year is when the Chabad rabbi took it over; Temple Judea itself is older and was not Chabad.

earlier.where: Temple Judea (a non-Chabad congregation, the same shul)

2750675.name: Yeshivah Torah Ohr
2750675.note: Chabad.org (CrownHeights.info, 28 Aug 2011): a student 'went to Miami last winter to study at a brand-new yeshiva for 10 days', leaving New Jersey 'at the end of December' (2010): 'Yeshiva Torah Ohr, a Chabad-Lubavitch run institution in North Miami Beach'; Rabbi Immanuel Storfer opened it after running the Miami Torah Experience for two winters. Brand new by December 2010; the exact opening is not stated.

3011301.name: Young Israel Chabad
3011301.note: Sun-Sentinel (CrownHeights.info, 3 Sept 2014): 'When the High Holidays begin in a few weeks, a Chabad Lubavitch rabbi will be on the bima at Young Israel of Pembroke Pines, which will be known as Young Israel/Chabad of Pembroke Pines. The Orthodox synagogue at Century Village introduced Rabbi Shimon Andrusier ... at an Aug. 24 open house.' The Young Israel shul itself opened in 1990 (its own site), not as Chabad.

earlier.where: Young Israel of Pembroke Pines, Century Village (the same shul, before it was Chabad)
